title: Marching tetrahedra opens the mesh where a floor on the lattice samples to both signs: the #4107 snap leaves a collinear facet that is dropped

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

A follow-up to #4107 / #4117 (ours). The snap in `tet` (`iso.rs`) is decided per edge: a crossing within `NODE_SNAP` of a sample, as a fraction of that edge's value span, sits on the sample. Where a floor lies on a lattice layer, the samples there read about +-1e-12 with both signs. Take a tetrahedron with two such samples `a` (inside) and `e` (outside) joined by an edge, plus one corner well inside and one well outside. The crossings on the long edges snap to `a` and to `e`. On the edge `a`-`e` both values are tiny, so its crossing stays mid-edge. The facet (`a`, crossing on `a`-`e`, `e`) has three distinct corners on one lattice edge, so its normal is exactly zero, and `push` drops it. Its three edges then lose one use each, and the mesh opens: 3 open edges per dropped facet.

Before #4117 the same facet was kept as a sliver about 1e-12 off the line. The mesh stayed closed, but the sliver counted as zero-area once the corners were welded.

Measured on main e6849c5ae, a synthetic box with its top face exactly on lattice layer 4 (step 0.25 mm). The top-layer samples are given noise of +-1e-12, both signs; every other sample is exact.

| | facets | `open_edges` | `unpaired_edges` | facets dropped with three distinct corners |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (per-edge snap) | 2,219 | 45 | 45 | 15 |
| `NODE_SNAP` = 0 (before #4117) | 3,104 | 0 | 515 | n/a |
| per-sample snap (below) | 1,808 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

With noise of one sign only, main gives 0 / 0. Our own lane, on cut stock at cell 0.254 mm after #4117, has 39, 48 and 24 open edges on three programs, all multiples of 3.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a `Grid` (step 0.25, `n` = [16, 16, 8]) of a box: x and y from 0.6 to 3.4, z from 0.35 to 1.0. The top face z = 1.0 is lattice layer k = 4. On that layer, give each sample +1e-12 where (7i + 13j) mod 3 = 0 and -1e-12 elsewhere (both signs). Every other sample is the exact box distance.
2. `marching(&grid)`.
3. `open_edges` is 45. Expected: 0.

### Proposed fix

Decide the snap per sample, not per edge. In `marching`, a sample within `NODE_SNAP * step` of zero is read as +0.0: on the surface, on the outside side of `d < 0`. That sample has one value in every tetrahedron that shares it, so an edge between two such samples has no crossing and no collinear facet can arise. The per-edge test in `cross` can then go, or stay as a harmless second guard. The surface moves at most `NODE_SNAP * step` (0.25 nm at a 0.25 mm step).

Tried on a probe: the box above extracts with 0 open, 0 unpaired and no near-zero facet. The `stock_sim::iso` lib tests (7) and `stock_dual` (7) pass. Pins: the box above, and the existing #4107 pins.

### Version and OS

main e6849c5ae (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P2` (a mesh the extractor produces fails the closed check).
